issues: HIGH: games.json assigns limited_attempts to Tetris, but the corpus describes spatial capacity, top-out, and escalating speed—not a budgeted number of actions or attempts as required by the library definition.

HIGH: Several normalized/provenance assignments overstate sequencing_dependency: PowerWash Simulator explicitly permits self-directed cleaning order without dependency-based failure, while Phoenix Wright largely follows a prescribed sequence rather than asking players to design one.

repair_actions.actions: Added layer field (challenge/modifier/motivation); moved score_optimization+collection_progression+persistent_learning to motivation layer (never substitutes for challenge); reframed persistent_learning failure_mode; added rule_matching_verification challenge mechanic (Papers Please / Ace Attorney / Obra Dinn / Zoombinis structures); removed loose mappings (Pokemon cooperative_coordination, PowerWash partial_information); evidence_games provenance now on all entries derived from corpus; job-mechanics-map regenerated over challenge+modifier only with motivation_layer listed separately.

Added execution_precision challenge mechanic (Cooking Mama/PowerWash execution-accuracy structures); fixed overstated provenance (Tetris off limited_attempts, Papers Please off spatial_optimization); clarified combination_search vs multiple_valid_solutions boundary. Acceptance-criteria correction: the review prompt demanded all-challenge entries, contradicting the project owner's Stage-2 spec which explicitly lists variable_conditions/multiple_valid_solutions/score_optimization/collection_progression/persistent_learning as library members — prompt now encodes the intentional 3-layer design and judges each entry against its own layer.
